ingredients.text: 10 tablespoons (140 g) unsalted butter room temperature
2 cups (250 g) all-purpose flour weighed in grams or spooned and leveled
¼ cup sliced almonds optional, for topping

steps.body: Preheat oven to 350°F.
In a large bowl, cream together the softened butter and sugar with a mixer on medium speed until light and fluffy (1-2 minutes). Mix in the egg and almond extract well.
Add the flour, baking soda, and salt to the wet ingredients and mix thoroughly to combine. Scrape the sides of the bowl as needed.
Scoop 3-4 tablespoons of dough, roll into a ball, and place on a baking sheet 2-3 inches apart. Bake until the edges just start to tan (about 9-12 minutes).
Let the cookies cool on the pan for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to finish cooling.
In a small bowl, make the icing by stirring together the powdered sugar, milk, and almond extract until smooth. Spread icing over the cooled cookies and top with a few sliced almonds.

ingredients.text: 4 tablespoons unsalted butter, at room temperature (56g)
12 tablespoons unsalted butter, at room temperature (170g)
1 large egg yolk, at room temperature

steps.body: Make the crumb topping: In a small bowl, whisk the flour, brown sugar, and cinnamon. Using a fork or a handheld mixer on low speed, mix in the butter until crumbly. Refrigerate the topping until the cookies are shaped.
Make the cookies: In a medium bowl, whisk the flour, cornstarch, baking powder, salt, and baking soda.

In a large bowl using a handheld or stand mixer fitted with the paddle, beat the butter, brown sugar, and granulated sugar on medium-high speed until the mixture is light and creamy, about 3 minutes. Add the egg, egg yolk, and vanilla and beat on high speed until combined, about 1 minute. Scrape down the sides of the bowl as needed. Add the flour mixture and beat on low speed until combined.
Cover the dough tightly and refrigerate it for at least 2 hours or up to 3 days.

Preheat the oven to 350°F (177°C). Line baking sheets with parchment paper or silicone baking mats. If the dough has chilled for longer than 2 hours, let it sit at room temperature for about 30 minutes.

Scoop and roll the chilled cookie dough into balls, about a scant 1½ tablespoons (30g) each. Using your fingers and thumbs, pinch and press a large indent in the center of the dough ball until it resembles a shallow bowl (1). Use the "bowl" of dough to scoop a generous amount of cold crumb topping to fill the cookie (2). Arrange them 3 inches apart on the prepared baking sheets (3).

Bake for 12 to 14 minutes or until the edges of the cookies are very lightly browned and set. Cool the cookies on the baking sheet for 10 minutes before transferring to a cooling rack to cool completely before icing.

Make the icing: In a small bowl, whisk the powdered sugar, 1 tablespoon milk, and vanilla. Add another tablespoon of milk to thin it out, if desired. Drizzle over the cooled cookies. The icing will set after about 2 hours. Store covered tightly at room temperature for up to 2 days or in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.

notes.author: celeste
notes.title: Meal Prep Advice from Gemini
notes.body:
Freeze the chicken after frying and without the sauce or onions.

Freezing raw, egg-and-flour coated chicken causes the batter to absorb moisture from the meat, turning into a soggy paste that will not fry properly from frozen. Commercial frozen chicken nuggets and tenders are always par-fried or fully fried before freezing for this exact reason.

Step-by-Step Meal Prep Strategy

- Fry completely (or par-fry): Fry the chicken pieces until they are cooked through and lightly golden. For an extra-crispy result upon reheating, use a 50/50 mix of cornstarch and flour in your dredge.
- Cool thoroughly: Let the fried chicken cool completely on a wire rack. Freezing warm chicken traps steam, creating ice crystals that ruin crispiness.
- Flash freeze to prevent clumping: Spread the cooled chicken pieces in a single layer on a parchment-lined baking sheet. Freeze for 1 to 2 hours until solid, then transfer them into a freezer bag or airtight container.
- Keep sauce and onions separate: Store the Panda Express orange sauce and sautéed onions separately (either in small freezer-safe containers or in the fridge if using within a week). Coating the chicken in sauce before freezing guarantees a mushy, soggy crust when reheated.

Best Reheating Methods

- Air Fryer (Best): Cook from frozen at 380°F (193°C) for 6–8 minutes (or 400°F / 204°C for 2–3 additional minutes to maximize crunch), shaking the basket halfway through.
- Oven: Bake from frozen on a wire rack set inside a baking sheet at 400°F (204°C) for 12–15 minutes until sizzling and crisp.
- Assembly: Warm the sauce and sautéed onions in a skillet or wok over medium heat. Once the chicken is hot and crispy from the air fryer or oven, immediately toss it into the sauce off the heat for 30–60 seconds so it gets evenly coated while staying crunchy.

notes.author: celeste
notes.title: How to make crispy reheated fried chicken advice from Gemini
notes.body:
The secret to keeping fried chicken crunchy under a wet, sugary glaze lies in minimizing gluten formation and reducing internal moisture in the crust.
Ingredient Upgrades
 * Cornstarch or Potato Starch (50% to 100% of dredge): All-purpose flour develops gluten when wet, creating a spongy structure that rapidly absorbs sauce. Pure starches contain no gluten and form a glass-like, rigid shell that resists moisture penetration.
 * Rice Flour: Replacing 20–30% of your flour with white rice flour creates an airy, brittle crunch (standard in Korean fried chicken).
 * Baking Powder: Adding 1/2 teaspoon per cup of dredge raises the pH and creates microscopic carbon dioxide bubbles during frying. This adds surface area and micro-pockets that stay shatteringly crisp.
 * Vodka or High-Proof Alcohol: If using a wet batter, substitute part of the water with vodka. Alcohol evaporates much faster than water in hot oil, dehydrating the crust faster and preventing gluten from forming.
Crucial Techniques
 * The Double-Fry Method:
   * First fry (325°F / 163°C for 3–4 mins): Cooks the meat through and drives out inner moisture.
   * Rest (5–10 mins on a wire rack): Allows remaining steam to migrate to the surface.
   * Second fry (375°F–390°F / 190°C–200°C for 1–2 mins): Instantly vaporizes surface moisture, creating a hard, blistered shell that stays crunchy far longer.
 * Drain on a Wire Rack (Never Paper Towels): Paper towels trap escaping steam underneath the pieces, softening the bottom crust within seconds.
 * Thicken the Sauce Properly: A watery sauce will immediately ruin a crust. Ensure the orange sauce is cooked down with enough cornstarch slurry so it coats the back of a spoon with a glossy, syrup-like consistency.
 * Flash-Toss Off the Heat: Never simmer fried chicken in the sauce. Bring the sauce to a bubbling glaze in the pan, turn the heat completely off, dump in the hot chicken, and toss for just 15–20 seconds to coat.

notes.author: jordan_cooks
notes.body: Air fryer reheat at 400°F kept them crunchy.

ingredients.text: 4 tbsp unsalted butter, melted and cooled slightly

steps.body: In the bowl of a stand mixer, combine the warm milk, yeast, and 1 teaspoon of the sugar. Let sit for 5–10 minutes until foamy.
Add the remaining sugar, melted butter, eggs, and vanilla extract. Whisk to combine.
Add 2 3/4 cups of flour and the salt. Using the dough hook attachment, mix on low speed until a soft dough forms.
Knead on medium-low speed for 5–7 minutes (or knead by hand on a lightly floured surface) until smooth and elastic. If too sticky, add the remaining 1/4 cup of flour 1 tablespoon at a time.
Shape the dough into a ball and place it in an oiled bowl, turning once to grease the top. Cover with plastic wrap or a clean towel and let rise in a warm place until doubled in size, about 1 hour.
Butter and lightly flour a 9x5-inch loaf pan.
In a small bowl, rub the orange zest into the granulated sugar and brown sugar using your fingers until fragrant. Stir in the cinnamon.
Punch down the dough and turn it out onto a lightly floured surface. Roll into approximately a 12x20-inch rectangle.
Brush the surface evenly with the 4 tablespoons of melted butter, then sprinkle the orange-cinnamon sugar evenly over the butter.
Cut the dough lengthwise into 6 equal strips. Stack the strips on top of each other, then cut the stack into 6 equal squares/rectangles (yielding 6 stacks of layered squares).
Layer the dough squares cut-side up (like index cards in a file box) into the prepared loaf pan.
Cover loosely and let rise again for 30–45 minutes, until puffy.
Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C).
Bake the loaf for 30–35 minutes, until golden brown on top and baked through the center. (If the top browns too quickly, tent loosely with aluminum foil for the last 10 minutes).
Let the bread cool in the pan on a wire rack for 10–15 minutes.
Meanwhile, whisk together the powdered sugar, orange juice, orange zest, and vanilla extract in a small bowl until smooth.
Drizzle the glaze generously over the warm bread and serve warm.

ingredients.text: ⅔ cup granulated sugar, divided (⅓ cup for dough, ⅓ cup for rolling)

steps.body: Whisk flour and baking soda together in a medium bowl. Set aside.
Beat together butter, peanut butter, brown sugar, ⅓ cup of the granulated sugar, and salt until well-combined and slightly lighter in color.
Beat in the egg and vanilla. Then add the flour mixture and mix until just combined.
If the dough is too sticky to roll, refrigerate for 15 minutes.
Put the remaining ⅓ cup granulated sugar in a bowl. Roll dough into balls, roll in the sugar, and arrange on a baking sheet.
Bake at 375°F for 8–10 minutes, until they look puffy and crackled and are just starting to brown on the bottom.
Immediately press one chocolate kiss on top of each cookie and allow to cool to doneness.

title: Salted Caramel Brownies
description: Rich, ultra-fudgy chocolate brownies layered and swirled with homemade salted caramel and topped with flaky sea salt.

ingredients.text: 6 tbsp (85g) unsalted butter, cut into cubes and at room temperature
1 tsp flaky sea salt (such as Maldon)
8 oz (225g) semi-sweet or bittersweet chocolate, roughly chopped

steps.body: Heat granulated sugar in a medium saucepan over medium-low heat, stirring constantly with a heatproof spatula or wooden spoon. The sugar will form clumps and eventually melt into a thick amber-colored liquid (keep a close eye so it doesn't burn).
Once the sugar is completely melted, carefully add the cubed butter. Whisk vigorously until the butter is fully melted and incorporated (the mixture will bubble vigorously).
Slowly drizzle in the heavy cream while continuing to whisk. Allow the mixture to boil for 1 minute.
Remove from heat and stir in the 1 tsp flaky sea salt. Set aside to cool slightly while you make the brownie batter.
Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C). Line a 9x9-inch metal baking pan with parchment paper, leaving an overhang on the sides for easy removal.
In a heatproof bowl set over a pot of simmering water (or in 30-second bursts in the microwave), melt the butter and chopped chocolate together until smooth and glossy. Set aside to cool slightly.
In a large bowl, whisk together the granulated sugar, brown sugar, eggs, and vanilla extract vigorously for 1–2 minutes until pale, frothy, and slightly thickened (this creates the crinkly top).
Slowly pour the melted chocolate-butter mixture into the egg mixture, whisking constantly until combined.
Sift in the flour, cocoa powder, and salt. Gently fold with a rubber spatula just until no dry flour streaks remain (do not overmix).
Pour roughly half of the brownie batter into the prepared baking pan and smooth into an even layer.
Drizzle about 1/3 to 1/2 cup of the salted caramel sauce evenly over the batter layer.
Pour the remaining brownie batter over the top, gently smoothing it out.
Spoon additional tablespoons of caramel over the top layer and use a butter knife or toothpick to gently swirl the caramel into the top batter. (Save any leftover caramel for serving).
Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 32–38 minutes, until the edges are set and a toothpick inserted into the center comes out with moist, fudgy crumbs (not wet batter).
Remove from the oven and immediately sprinkle generously with flaky sea salt.
Allow the brownies to cool completely in the pan at room temperature before slicing for clean cuts.

notes.author: celeste
notes.body: Room Temperature Dairy: Ensure your butter and heavy cream for the caramel are at room temperature to avoid seizing the melted sugar.

notes.author: celeste
notes.body: Clean Slices: For ultra-clean bakery-style cuts, chill the fully-cooled brownies in the refrigerator for 1–2 hours before slicing with a sharp chef's knife wiped clean between cuts.

notes.author: celeste
notes.body: Pan Type: Use a light-colored metal pan rather than glass, as glass retains heat unevenly and can cause the edges to overbake before the center sets.

title: Stovetop Popcorn
description: A classic, foolproof method for making light, crispy, and perfectly popped popcorn on the stove without burnt kernels.

ingredients.text: 2–3 tbsp high-smoke point oil (such as coconut oil, avocado oil, or canola oil)
1/2–1 tsp fine sea salt or popcorn salt
Optional flavorings: Nutritional yeast, smoked paprika, garlic powder, or grated parmesan

steps.body: Test the Oil: Add the oil and 3–4 "test" kernels to the pot. Cover with the lid and place over medium-high heat.
Wait for the Test Kernels: When the test kernels pop, the oil is at the ideal temperature. Remove the popped test kernels with a spoon or tongs.

Even Heating: Add the remaining 1/3 cup of kernels in a single, even layer. Cover the pot and immediately remove it from the heat for 30 seconds (this brings all kernels up to near-popping temperature so they pop at the same time and don't burn).

Pop the Corn: Return the pot to medium-high heat. Keep the lid slightly cracked/ajar to allow steam to escape (this keeps the popcorn light and crisp rather than chewy). Shake the pot gently back and forth over the burner while the corn pops.

Remove from Heat: Once the popping slows to roughly 2–3 seconds between pops, remove the pot immediately from the heat. Remove the lid and dump the popcorn into your serving bowl right away to prevent trapped steam or scorching at the bottom.
Season and Serve: Drizzle warm melted butter over the top and toss thoroughly. Sprinkle fine salt and desired seasonings, tossing gently until evenly coated.

equipment: Large, heavy-bottomed pot with a lid (approx. 3–4 quarts)

notes.author: celeste
notes.body: Vent Steam: Leaving the lid slightly cracked while popping allows steam to escape, which is the secret to extra-crispy stovetop popcorn.

notes.author: celeste
notes.body: Fine Salt: Use fine table salt or grind sea salt with a mortar and pestle or spice grinder so it clings to the kernels better.

notes.author: celeste
notes.body: Oil Choice: Coconut oil gives the most authentic movie-theater flavor, while ghee or clarified butter adds a rich, buttery taste without burning.

notes.author: sam_eats
notes.body: Coconut oil really does taste like the movies.

Whisk the eggs, sugar, flour, lemon juice, and zest until smooth.
Pour over the hot crust and bake 20 minutes more, until set.
Cool completely, chill, then dust with powdered sugar and cut into bars.
Cook the onion in oil until golden, then add the garlic and ginger.
Stir in the garam masala and cumin for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and chickpeas and simmer 20 minutes, mashing a few chickpeas to thicken.
Season with salt and serve over rice with cilantro.
Blend everything until smooth.
Taste, add more sugar if needed, and serve cold.
Mash the avocados with the lime juice and salt.
Fold in the onion, jalapeno, cilantro, and tomato.
Taste, adjust the salt and lime, and serve right away.
